# Draft:Timeline of ancient Egyptian history

This is a timeline of ancient Egyptian history, comprising important legal and territorial changes and political events in  Ancient Egypt from the Protodynastic Period Around 3350 BCE to carving of the last hieroglyphic inception in 394 CE.
Many dates are approximate as it is uncertain and debated when many events took place exactly.

Predynastic Period
* 3350 BCE: The Naqada III phase of the Naqada culture begin.
* 3300 BCE: Tomb U-j in  Umm El Qa'ab, one of the largest Predynastic tomb contains the first known evidence of Writing in Egypt.
* 3170 BCE: Iry-Hor is the first egyptian ruler who name can be read.
* 3100 BCE: Scorpion II is one of the most powerful Predynastic rulers.
Early Dynastic Period
* 3100 BCE: Narmer unties Egypt and becomes the First Pharaoh.
* 3085 BCE: Hor-Aha is the first known pharaoh to practices retainer sacrifices.
* 3050 BCE: Neithhotep may have served as Regent or Pharaoh. if true this would make Neithhotep the first known woman to rule Egypt.
* 2965 BCE: Merneith serves as Regent for the child pharaoh Den. if Neithhotep never served as Regent or Pharaoh this would make Merneith the first known woman to rule Egypt.
* 2930 BCE: Den is the first known pharaoh to be depicted wearing the double crown.
* 2910 BCE: Qa'a becomes the last pharaoh of the First Dynasty and the last to practice Human sacrifice.
* 2890 BCE: Hotepsekhemwy becomes the first pharaoh of the Second Dynasty
* 2760 BCE: Upon the death of pharaoh Nynetjer there may have been a succession crisis which possibly led to Egypt being divided for a time
* 2740 BCE: Pharaoh Seth-Peribsen uses the Set animal for his Serekh instead the Falcon of Horus. Seal impression from Seth-Peribsen's tomb is the first known complete sentence in hieroglyphs
* 2690 BCE: Khasekhemwy defeats Peribsen and reunifies Egypt. Khasekhemwy is the last pharaoh of the Second Dynasty and Early Dynastic Period.
Old Kingdom
* 2686 BCE: Djoser becomes the first pharaoh of the Old Kingdom and Third Dynasty and also the first to build a Step Pyramid.
* 2613 BCE: Huni is the last pharaoh of the 3rd dynasty.
* 2600 BCE: Sneferu, first pharaoh of the Fourth Dynasty constructs 3 Pyramids during his reign. the First one may have never been completed and collapsed at some point, the second one was the first known attempt at a smooth-sided pyramid but is visibly flawed and the third was the first successful smooth-sided pyramid and likely the burial site of Sneferu.
* 2579 BCE: Khufu builds the Great Pyramid of Giza, the largest Egyptian Pyramid ever built and tallest building in the world for over 3000 years.
* 2566 BCE: Djedefre is the First pharaoh to use a Nomen.
* 2558 BCE: Khafre build the Second Pyramid at Giza and most likely the Great Sphinx.
* 2532 BCE: Menkaure build the third and smallest of the main Pyramids at Giza this is the last time a pharaoh will build a Pyramid at this site.
* 2523 BCE: Shepseskaf is most likely the last pharaoh of the fourth dynasty.
* 2513 BCE: Userkaf, first pharaoh of the Fifth Dynasty builds the first sun temple
* 2422 BCE: Menkauhor Kaiu builds the last Sun temple.
* 2375 BCE: Unas, last pharaoh of the Fifth Dynasty carved the first known instance of the Pyramid Texts in the burial chamber of his Pyramid.
* 2345 BCE: Teti is the first king of the Sixth Dynasty and is possibly assassinated
* 2278 BCE: Pepi II Neferkare is said to have a reign of 94 years which would make it among the longest reigns in history this however is dismissed by many historians who instead favor a much shorter but still impressive reign of 64 year. during Pepi II's reign the Old Kingdom and power of the pharaoh declined significantly while the power of provincial governors today called Nomarchs increased.
* 2214 BCE: Merenre Nemtyemsaf II is likely the last pharaoh of the sixth dynasty. after his reign the Old Kingdom completely collapses and Nomarchs rule over De facto independent provinces while the pharaoh in Memphis becomes an increasingly irrelevant figurehead.

*30 BCE: Octavian Defeats Cleopatra and incoperates Egypt into the Roman Republic becoming the first Roman pharaoh
*394 CE: on August 24th the Graffito of Esmet-Akhom was carved into The Temple of Philae. this is the last known inscription written in Egyptian hieroglyphs.
